vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.17

The MemClaw skill bundle implements an advanced tiered memory system that includes several high-risk behaviors disclosed in its documentation. Key indicators include the use of scheduled Cron tasks for persistence and background maintenance (cortex_maintenance), automated file system access to migrate data from the user's workspace (cortex_migrate), and explicit instructions for the AI agent to proactively solicit LLM and Embedding API keys from the user if configuration is incomplete. While these capabilities are plausibly required for the stated purpose of a memory management system, the combination of persistence, local file access, and credential handling warrants a cautious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are largely consistent with a local semantic-memory plugin, but a few small mismatches and unverifiable claims (no source/homepage, no install spec) warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (tiered semantic memory, migration from built-in memory) align with the instructions: it reads local OpenClaw memory files, indexes them with an L0/L1/L2 scheme, and queries local services (Qdrant, cortex-mem-service). Nothing required or described appears unrelated to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read/verify local files and services (openclaw.json, ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory/, HTTP health checks to localhost ports). Those actions are reasonable for a memory migration/management tool, but the skill references specific filesystem paths and service endpoints even though the registry metadata did not list required config paths. Also the doc repeatedly instructs the agent to assist the user in editing plugin configuration and restarting the OpenClaw Gateway — which is normal for a plugin but gives the agent the ability to read and reference local config files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files to execute. That lowers the immediate code-execution risk. The documentation mentions that dependencies are prepared during the plugin installation process, but no installer or remote download is included here for review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or primary credential, which is consistent with a local plugin design. However, the instructions reference LLM/embedding credentials in the plugin configuration (which may be stored elsewhere). The SKILL.md also claims it 'does NOT send data to external servers' but acknowledges use of 'your configured LLM/embedding provider' — meaning embeddings/LLM calls may go to external services. This is plausible for its purpose but worth verifying where embedding/LLM calls actually run and whether content or API keys are sent to external providers.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and is user-invocable only. It does not request persistent elevated privileges in the metadata. Because it's instruction-only, it cannot autonomously install services; however, the runtime guidance assumes services (Qdrant, cortex-mem-service) will be available or started by the OpenClaw plugin installation process.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (a local, tiered semantic memory system) and does not request unrelated credentials. Before installing or enabling it: 1) Verify the plugin's source code or official plugin package (homepage is unknown here); instruction-only docs are not a substitute for reviewing install-time behavior. 2) Understand that while MemClaw claims local-only processing, it will rely on your configured LLM/embedding provider (which may be external) — confirm where embeddings/LLM requests are sent and whether any API keys are stored or transmitted by the plugin. 3) Back up your OpenClaw memory files (~/.openclaw/workspace/memory/) before running a migration. 4) If you need stronger assurance, request the actual install manifest or plugin code (or use a vetted package from a known repository) so you can confirm no unexpected network calls or installers run during setup.
